title: Sterilization Practices

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Physical or chemical processes intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life, including bacterial endospores, from an item or material.
explanation: Common sterilization methods in a teaching/basic microbiology lab include moist heat (autoclaving) and, for some heat-sensitive items, filtration or chemical sterilants. The specific cycle parameters needed to achieve sterility depend on the load type, volume, and container — a single universal time/temperature/pressure combination should not be assumed for every load; validated cycle parameters and periodic verification (see Sterilization Indicators) confirm actual performance.
keyPractices: Match the sterilization method to the material (e.g. moist heat for most media and heat-stable items; filtration for heat-labile liquids).
Do not assume a single fixed cycle works for every load size/type — verify against the equipment manual and load validation.
Use appropriate indicators to periodically verify sterilization efficacy (see the Sterilization Indicators concept entry).
commonMistakes: Assuming the same autoclave cycle used for a small tube is adequate for a much larger liquid volume without verification.
